symptom: `mxcli check script.mdl -p app.mpr` printed "Check passed!" for a script that `mxcli exec` on the same project then refused for the project's Mendix version, after running the statements before the refused one (on a 9.24 project: `create view entity` -> "create view entity requires Mendix 10.18.0+"; the issue's own StableId/CaseValues refusal was the write-time property floor, already cured by #1410)
cause: Every version gate exec applies lived inline in its handler as a checkFeature(ctx, area, name, …) call — about two dozen across 17 files, several conditional on the statement's content (send email in the body, a page with parameters, SupportsGraphQL, a timer event sub-process). check -p and exec's pre-flight never run a handler, so neither could see a gate: the project version was consulted only when the handler ran.
file: `mdl/executor/version_gates.go` (statementVersionGates: the one statement-to-feature table; checkVersionGates for the handlers; Executor.CheckVersionGates -> MDL-VERSION01 for `cmd/mxcli/cmd_check.go` and `cmd/mxcli/exec_preflight.go`); the handlers in cmd_*.go now call checkVersionGates(ctx, stmt)
insight: A refusal only a handler can raise is a check/exec gap by construction (duplicate-resolver-drift, check versus exec): move the decision into a pure function of the statement that the handler and the pre-flight both call, rather than giving check a second copy. TestCheckFeatureIsOnlyCalledFromTheGateTable fails on any new direct checkFeature call, so a future gate cannot bypass the table. Two kinds stay exec-only: gates that depend on stored state (drop/alter of a message definition document that is not there) and the write-time property floor (canon.StripUndeclaredProperties), which needs the encoded BSON and is cured by the writer emitting the version's shape (#1410), not by a check rule. Fixture for any Mendix 9 check: modelsdk/mpr/testdata/v1-project/App.mpr is 9.24.30.
